en: Artifacts are checksummed, not signed: per-artifact sha256 and size sit in releases/<tag>.json and latest.json and are checked by verify_checksum in site/static/install.sh:478 (called at :706); SHA256SUMS is uploaded to the GitHub release (.github/workflows/release.yml). There is no signature, attestation or Sigstore, and docs/DISTRIBUTION.md:151-153 records that as deferred on purpose. A checksum fetched from the same origin as the archive proves integrity in transit, not provenance. The pack's premise that releases are signed is false, as is its premise that majordomus update is a self-updater: it regenerates provider projections (lib/update.sh:4), and there is no self-update command (docs/DISTRIBUTION.md:416-439). Lowest priority because the deferral is a recorded decision. Baseline audit of 2026-10-09 at master 1fb8d6be44, failure gap 12 and premises 1-2.
cs: Artefakty mají kontrolní součty, nejsou podepsané: sha256 a velikost každého artefaktu jsou v releases/<tag>.json a latest.json a kontroluje je verify_checksum v site/static/install.sh:478 (volané na :706); SHA256SUMS se nahrává do GitHub release (.github/workflows/release.yml). Není tu žádný podpis, atestace ani Sigstore a docs/DISTRIBUTION.md:151-153 zaznamenává, že je to odloženo záměrně. Kontrolní součet stažený ze stejného původu jako archiv dokazuje integritu při přenosu, ne původ. Předpoklad balíčku, že release jsou podepsané, je nepravdivý, stejně jako jeho předpoklad, že majordomus update je self-updater: přegenerovává projekce providerů (lib/update.sh:4) a žádný příkaz self-update neexistuje (docs/DISTRIBUTION.md:416-439). Nejnižší priorita, protože odložení je zaznamenané rozhodnutí. Základní audit z 2026-10-09 na masteru 1fb8d6be44, mezera selhání 12 a předpoklady 1-2.

Readiness is decided independently by <t9/> (the producer's output exists, <t10/>), by <t11/> (<t12/>, <t13/>) and by <t14/>'s bare TCP connect (<t15/>); the lease probe uses a fourth question, <t16/> plus the identity digest (<t17/>), and none of them asks the version. There is no <t18/>, <t19/>, <t20/> or <t21/> for the server in the executable (<t22/>), and the shell tool's <t23/> does not know the lease exists (<t24/>). Since: the lease is one type read once and <t25/> serves it, with <t26/>/<t27/>/<t28/> on the executable (stage 02, 03); <t29/> carries a <t30/> check decided by that same reading, so the report names the address, the version and whether what answers is the code on disk, and a stale lease is a finding rather than a silence (stage 09, <t31/>). The readiness answers are named rather than merged: four questions about four subjects, each pointed at its owner in <t32/> ("Four readings of "ready"") and in the module doc where the four meet (<t33/>). The shell tool's <t34/> still does not know the lease exists. Reproduce: <t35/>; <t36/>.
